subject: Week 28: stranger anxiety peaks - brief the Thanksgiving table
bodyText:
This week
Stranger anxiety is entering its early peak, and it shares machinery with this week's cognitive work: Avi now searches for partially hidden objects, which means he also knows familiar people still exist when they leave the room. Rocking on hands and knees is emerging for some, with first crawl steps possible; finding fully hidden objects is a roughly 9-month attainment, so half-hidden is the right game this week. Expect extended babble strings, including vocalizing when he is alone.

Watch-fors this week
- [low concern] Crying at unfamiliar adults and clinging at daycare drop-off - normal attachment behavior at 7-9 months, not a social red flag.
- [low concern] Refusing a new solid on first offer - acceptance averages 5-10 exposures; keep offering without pressure.
- [monitor] Sustained refusal of all unfamiliar caregivers beyond the typical 2-5 minute adjustment - document it and raise if it persists.
- [call within 24h] Hives spreading beyond the mouth area, vomiting within 2 hours, or lethargy after a newly introduced food.
- [call now] Fever at or above 102F (rectal) with lethargy, labored breathing, or blue lips - call 911.

Enrichment opportunities
- Half-hide a toy under a burp cloth and let him find it, then graduate to fully hidden once he solves it reliably - object permanence is consolidating now, and peek-a-boo is at peak developmental value. CDC 9-month milestones: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/9-months.html
- Brief Thanksgiving relatives before they arrive: give Avi 15 minutes of warm-up at floor level before anyone picks him up, and keep the handoff ritual scripted and decisive - lingering goodbyes intensify the distress. AAP developmental milestones, 7 months: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/ages-stages/baby/Pages/Developmental-Milestones-7-Months.aspx
- Keep every introduced allergen in rotation at 2-3 exposures weekly - the LEAP follow-up data show maintenance, not first introduction, is what sustains tolerance. Thin peanut butter into oatmeal, fold yogurt into fruit, flake salmon into a vegetable mash. AAP Starting Solid Foods: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/ages-stages/baby/feeding-nutrition/Pages/Starting-Solid-Foods.aspx
- Decide the movement-gym question once and move on: no evidence shows structured infant gym classes beat floor time, so buy one for logistics and parent community or skip the domain at zero measurable cost. The rational entry is Recess Collective in the Outer Sunset - dedicated 0-18-month zone, roughly $89 a month per family. Recess Collective: https://recesscollective.org/

Upcoming
- Day 208-214 (week of Dec 5, 2026): if he pulls to stand, the crib mattress drops to its lowest setting that same day - pre-position the plan now.
- Day 215-221 (week of Dec 12, 2026): the 8/9-month sleep-regression window opens - mobility surge plus separation cognition drives night wakings; hold the sleep practices that already work.

Developmental milestone check-in
Tap any link to mark it complete. View or change others at https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones

- Responds to other people's emotional expressions
  AAP window: day 180-270
  What to look for: Crying when a parent is sad, brightening when a parent laughs. Foundation of empathy.
  Source: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/ages-stages/baby/Pages/Developmental-Milestones-7-Months.aspx
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/responds-to-others-emotions/complete

- Distinguishes emotions by tone of voice
  AAP window: day 180-270
  What to look for: Reacts differently to a stern vs warm voice with the same words.
  Source: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/ages-stages/baby/Pages/Developmental-Milestones-7-Months.aspx
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/distinguishes-emotion-tone/complete

- Finds a partially hidden object
  AAP window: day 180-270
  What to look for: Beginning of object permanence — fully hidden objects come later.
  Source: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/ages-stages/baby/Pages/Developmental-Milestones-7-Months.aspx
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/finds-partially-hidden-object/complete

- Struggles to reach objects that are out of reach
  AAP window: day 180-270
  What to look for: Goal-directed behavior. Often precedes intentional rolling or scooting toward an object.
  Source: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/ages-stages/baby/Pages/Developmental-Milestones-7-Months.aspx
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/struggles-for-out-of-reach/complete

- Begins to respond to the word 'no'
  AAP window: day 180-270
  What to look for: Pauses briefly when the word is said. Compliance is a much later milestone.
  Source: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/ages-stages/baby/Pages/Developmental-Milestones-7-Months.aspx
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/responds-to-no/complete
